passage: I'm Bidisha, and for a while after Baba moved out, my mother Lakshmi started using me as a go-between. "Tell your father the money is late again." "Ask him who lives in that flat with him." At night she'd say things like, "He never cared about us. You see that, don't you?" I felt sick every time, as if I had to pick a side and carry the messages between them. One evening I said, as gently as I could, "Ma, I love you both. I can't carry messages or report on Baba. You can call him yourself." She went quiet and cross. When it kept happening, I told my aunt at school, who is our counsellor, and she helped me find words to say it again, kindly but clearly.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi tell Bidisha to ask about the flat?
qa.a: She told Bidisha to ask him who lived in that flat with him.

qa.q: How did Bidisha feel when Lakshmi asked for messages to be carried and for agreement that Baba never cared?
qa.a: Bidisha felt sick and pulled between them, as if forced to choose a side.

qa.q: What did Bidisha do to handle the pressure?
qa.a: Bidisha kindly refused to carry messages or report, said "I love you both", and told a trusted adult when it continued. 🤍

qa.q: How might Lakshmi have been feeling when she asked Bidisha to carry messages?
qa.a: Likely hurt, angry and lonely herself, which does not make it Bidisha's job, and which may be why she went quiet and cross when refused.

grounding: Shows a teen used as messenger and spy by a parent who badmouths the other, kindly refusing and telling a trusted adult.

passage:
Visiting Sunday at the hostel always smelled of samosas and boot polish. Hrithik's father, Jagdish, took him to the bench behind the basketball court.
"Next time you're home," Papa said, low, "find out if your mother's spending on that new tuition centre she keeps talking about. And tell her I'm not paying for anything extra. She'll listen to you."
Hrithik's stomach dropped. It was the third message this month. "Papa, I can't do that. I don't want to be in the middle."
"You're my son. Whose side are you on?"
"Nobody's. I love you both. Please talk to her yourself."
Papa went silent and left early. That evening Hrithik knocked on the housemaster's door. Mr Bose listened to all of it, then said, "It's not your job to carry messages, and it's not your fault. I'll speak to the counsellor tomorrow, and we'll call both your parents together."

qa.q: Where did Hrithik and his father sit on visiting Sunday?
qa.a: On the bench behind the basketball court.

qa.q: How did Hrithik feel when Papa asked him to spy on his mother?
qa.a: He felt sick and trapped between his parents; his stomach dropped because it was the third such message this month.

qa.q: Which steps protected Hrithik, and what did Mr Bose add?
qa.a: He refused kindly and told a trusted adult the same day; Mr Bose told him it was not his job or fault and planned to involve the counsellor and both parents.

qa.q: How might Jagdish see Hrithik's refusal?
qa.a: He seems hurt and frustrated, treating the refusal as disloyalty, possibly because his own anger at the divorce blinds him to the pressure on his son.

grounding: A teen whose father uses him as messenger and spy kindly refuses and tells a trusted adult, who reassures him it is not his job or fault.

passage:
Dear Abba,
I'm writing this instead of saying it on the phone, because on the phone my voice goes wrong.
Every weekend you ask me what Ammi bought, who visited, whether she goes out. Then you tell me things about her that make my chest hurt. Last Saturday you asked me to give her a message about the rent, and when I did, she cried in the kitchen and I felt like it was my fault.
I love you. I love Ammi. I'm not going to carry messages any more, and I'm not going to report on her house. Please ask her yourself, or through the lawyer.
I've told Nani about this, because it was getting too heavy. She said she will talk to both of you this week.
I still want our Sunday cricket. I just want to be your son there, not your spy.
Zubin

qa.q: What message did Zubin carry to Ammi last Saturday?
How did Zubin feel after passing the rent message?
qa.a: Zubin felt guilty and hurt; when Ammi cried in the kitchen, it felt like Zubin's fault, and the questions made Zubin's chest hurt.

qa.q: What makes Zubin's letter a wise response?
qa.a: It kindly but clearly refuses to carry messages or report, says Zubin loves both parents, and shows Zubin has told Nani, a trusted adult.

qa.q: What might Abba feel when he reads the letter?
qa.a: He may feel stung and ashamed at first, then possibly relieved that Zubin still wants their Sunday cricket and only asks to stop being a spy.

grounding: A teen writes to his father refusing to act as messenger or spy between divorcing parents and tells his grandmother about the pressure.
